history.period: Lake and garden begun 1750; temple built 1784
history.summary: The 'Ganpati of the lake' on an island in the 25-acre Sarasbaug garden. After completing the Devdeveshwar temple on Parvati hill, Nanasaheb Peshwa (Balaji Baji Rao) had a lake excavated at its base from 1750, retaining a ~25,000 sq ft island for a garden he named 'Saras Baug'. In 1784 Sawai Madhavrao Peshwa built a small temple on the island and installed the idol of Shree Siddhivinayak Gajanan, the deity he worshipped. The temple was used by the Marathas for confidential military strategy meetings against the Nizam and the British - the Peshwa and his commanders would be rowed into the lake, reportedly by non-Marathi-speaking boatmen for secrecy. Renovated many times (last major renovation 1969); a new white-marble idol by Rajasthani artisans was installed in 1990, and a small museum of Ganesha idols was added in 1995. Maintained by Shri Devdeveshwar Sansthan.

name: Sarasbaug Ganpati Temple
town_description: Pune is Maharashtra's second-largest city and the former seat of the Maratha Peshwas, often called the state's cultural capital and the 'Oxford of the East' for its many universities and research institutes. It is today a major IT, automotive and manufacturing hub. Its old-city core around Shaniwar Wada, the Peshwa-era temples and the Parvati hill is dense with historic and religious landmarks.

travel.road: Bajirao Road, Sarasbaug, near Swargate and Nehru Stadium; free entry to garden and temple

visitor_information.best_time: Year-round; early morning or sunset by the lake; Diwali Padwa deepotsav draws crowds
